meta.description: Read and print all card-to-account cross-reference records from the cross-reference file as a batch reporting/audit utility.
meta.process_description: This batch program sequentially reads every record in the card account cross-reference file (XREFFILE), which maps credit card numbers to their associated account identifiers. For each record found, it displays the cross-reference data to the system output (SYSOUT/job log), effectively producing a full listing of all card-to-account linkages held in the system. The program processes all records from start to finish in sequential order and terminates cleanly after the last record is read. If any file I/O error occurs during open, read, or close operations, the program abends with a standard error code (999) to signal the failure to operations staff.

files.XREFFILE: Card-to-account cross-reference master file (VSAM KSDS) that links each credit card number to its associated account record, enabling lookups between card numbers and account identifiers

business_rules: Every card-to-account cross-reference record in the file must be read and reported — no filtering or selection criteria are applied; this is a full file dump.
The credit card number (16 digits) is the unique key for each cross-reference record and determines the sequential read order.
If the cross-reference file cannot be opened, read, or closed successfully, the program must abend immediately with code 999 — no partial or silent failures are permitted.
End-of-file is a normal and expected condition (status '10') and does not constitute an error; all other non-zero statuses are treated as processing failures.
The program is read-only — it does not create, update, or delete any records, ensuring the integrity of the cross-reference data is preserved during the reporting run.

variables.name: FD-XREFFILE-REC
variables.description: Business meaning: The physical layout of a single record as it is read from the card-to-account cross-reference file. This is the raw file buffer that holds one cross-reference entry at a time during the batch read process, structured as a card number followed by its associated account data.

variables.name: FD-XREF-CARD-NUM
variables.description: Business meaning: The 16-digit credit card number as physically stored in the cross-reference file record. This is the unique identifier for each card in the file and serves as the primary key that determines the sequential order in which cards are read and reported during the batch run.

variables.name: FD-XREF-DATA
variables.description: Business meaning: The 34-character block of account reference data associated with the credit card number in the cross-reference file. This contains the customer and account identifiers that link the card to its owner and account, enabling the system to resolve a card number to a specific account relationship.

variables.name: XREFFILE-STATUS
variables.description: Business meaning: The two-character status code returned by the operating system after every file operation (open, read, close) on the cross-reference file. This is the primary indicator of whether each file interaction succeeded, reached end-of-file, or encountered an error that would require the batch job to abend.

variables.name: XREFFILE-STAT1
variables.description: Business meaning: The first character of the cross-reference file status code, representing the primary outcome category of the last file operation — for example, '0' indicates success, '1' indicates end-of-file, and '9' indicates a critical system-level error requiring immediate abend.

variables.name: XREFFILE-STAT2
variables.description: Business meaning: The second character of the cross-reference file status code, providing additional detail about the outcome of the last file operation. Combined with XREFFILE-STAT1, it allows the program to precisely distinguish between conditions such as normal end-of-file ('10') versus other non-zero error states that signal a processing failure.

variables.name: IO-STATUS
variables.description: Business meaning: A general-purpose two-character I/O status holder used to capture and evaluate file operation results in a standardized way across the program. It supports the error-handling logic that determines whether the batch job can continue processing cross-reference records or must abend.

variables.name: IO-STAT1
variables.description: Business meaning: The first character of the general I/O status code, indicating the high-level result category of a file operation. A value of '0' means the operation completed successfully; any other value triggers error evaluation to determine whether the batch run must be terminated.

variables.name: IO-STAT2
variables.description: Business meaning: The second character of the general I/O status code, providing granular detail about the file operation result. Together with IO-STAT1, it enables precise classification of file conditions, such as distinguishing a normal end-of-file from an unexpected read failure.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-BINARY
variables.description: Business meaning: A two-byte binary work area used to convert the two-character file status code into a numeric value for arithmetic comparison or display. This allows the program to evaluate and report file status codes in a consistent numeric format during error handling.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-ALPHA
variables.description: Business meaning: An alternate character-based view of the same two-byte work area used by TWO-BYTES-BINARY. This redefinition allows the program to load the two-character file status code into the binary field character by character, enabling conversion between the text status code and its numeric equivalent for error reporting.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-LEFT
variables.description: Business meaning: Holds the first character of the file status code when loading it into the binary conversion work area. This corresponds to the primary status category character (e.g., '0' for success, '1' for end-of-file) and is used as part of the status-to-numeric conversion for error diagnosis.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-RIGHT
variables.description: Business meaning: Holds the second character of the file status code when loading it into the binary conversion work area. This provides the secondary detail of the status (e.g., '0' for normal end-of-file when combined with '1') and completes the two-character status representation used in error diagnosis.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-04
variables.description: Business meaning: A structured numeric representation of the file status code, broken into its two component digits for precise error classification. This is used to interpret and display the exact file status when a cross-reference file operation fails, supporting auditability of batch errors.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0401
variables.description: Business meaning: The numeric equivalent of the first character of the file status code, initialized to zero (success). This represents the primary outcome category of the file operation and is used in error reporting to communicate the high-level nature of any cross-reference file failure.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0403
variables.description: Business meaning: The numeric equivalent of the second character of the file status code, initialized to zero (success). This provides the detailed sub-code of the file operation result and is used alongside IO-STATUS-0401 to produce a full, human-readable error status for diagnosing cross-reference file failures during the batch run.

variables.name: APPL-RESULT
variables.description: Business meaning: The internal application-level result code that classifies the outcome of each cross-reference file operation into one of three business states: success (continue processing), end-of-file (all records have been reported), or error (abend required). This drives the main control flow of the batch reporting job.

variables.name: APPL-AOK
variables.description: Business meaning: A condition name that evaluates to true when the last cross-reference file operation completed successfully. When active, it signals that the program should continue reading and reporting the next card-to-account cross-reference record.

variables.name: APPL-EOF
variables.description: Business meaning: A condition name that evaluates to true when all cross-reference records have been read and the end of the file has been reached. This is a normal, expected business condition signaling that the full file dump is complete and the program should proceed to close the file and end the batch run.

variables.name: END-OF-FILE
variables.description: Business meaning: A flag that tracks whether all card-to-account cross-reference records have been processed. Initialized to 'N' (not finished), it is set to 'Y' when the end-of-file condition is detected, causing the main read loop to stop and the batch report to conclude.

variables.name: ABCODE
variables.description: Business meaning: The abend code (set to 999) passed to the system abend handler when an unrecoverable error occurs during cross-reference file processing. Its presence in the job output signals to operations staff that the batch run failed due to a critical file I/O error and requires investigation before re-running.

variables.name: TIMING
variables.description: Business meaning: A numeric work field used to support timing or sequencing operations within the batch program, potentially used to measure or record elapsed processing time for performance monitoring of the cross-reference file reporting run.

paragraphs.name: 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the next credit card-to-account cross-reference record from the master file and immediately reports it to the job log. It also classifies the outcome as a successful read, a normal end-of-file, or an unrecoverable error, triggering an immediate abend if the file cannot be read.

paragraphs.name: 0000-XREFFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the card-to-account cross-reference file in preparation for the full audit listing run. If the file cannot be opened for any reason, the program immediately halts with a fatal error to prevent any silent or partial reporting failure.

paragraphs.name: 9000-XREFFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the card-to-account cross-reference file at the end of the reporting run, ensuring all system resources are properly released. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program immediately abends with a fatal error to alert operations staff of the failure.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles unrecoverable file processing failures by immediately terminating the program in a controlled abend, signalling to operations staff that a critical error has occurred and that the cross-reference report is incomplete and unreliable.

paragraphs.name: 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph formats and displays a human-readable file error status code to the job log whenever a file operation fails, giving operations staff the precise technical error detail needed to diagnose and resolve the cross-reference file processing failure.
